summary: In our Analog Atlas, we provided an intuitive user interface that allows the user to edit relevant environmental factors and match relevant landing sites on Mars and the Moon.  Previously , researchers and enthusiasts alike would need to spend many hours researching places of interest that would match their specific conditions. Using our website, the user can input their desired conditions into sliders, and the matching engine will find relevant and comparable places on Earth. Our tool is important to address the complexity of finding landing bases. Because Earth is over 196,000,000 square miles, there are millions of possibilities to consider. Furthermore, many of these locations are irrelevant, while only a handful should be taken into consideration. Our tool simply narrows the vast number of possibilities into a simple list of suitable locations.
details: Our Analog Atlas works by using factors such steepness, roughness, temperature, ground ice, and other parameters, all to calculate a score for 500 predetermined locations based on selected options that the user wants. This app mainly benefits people looking to speed up their research process in determining best launch locations by tailoring directly to their needs and wants. They no longer have to sift through thousands of candidates and quickly find the best option. In our project, we used Javascript for the frontend and Python for the backend to create the actual webapp, and used Claude AI to speed up production. We believe our project is creative because we haven't seen an all in one style project that addresses these specific objectives and takes into account complex parameters. When brainstorming ideas, we believed that speed is a large hurdle for many researchers and decided that it would be the factor to target.
